source_description: Sanitized diagnostic_state values extracted from user-provided v1.5.2 Test 3 bundle; no case identifier or free-form user messages

before_research.case_summary: PyTorch reports CUDA unavailable on a Windows 11 computer with an NVIDIA GTX 1080. The installed PyTorch build is CPU-only, which explains the reported symptom.
observations: The reported GPU is an NVIDIA GTX 1080.
The diagnostic ran in the affected Python environment.
torch.version.cuda is None and torch.version.hip is None.
No NVIDIA driver changes or PyTorch reinstallation have been made.

tests_performed.result: torch: 2.14.0+cpu; CUDA build: None; HIP build: None; CUDA available: False; device count: 0; first device: none.
tests_performed.test: PyTorch GPU runtime details in the affected environment

hypotheses.name: The installed PyTorch build is CPU-only
hypotheses.rationale: The +cpu version suffix and torch.version.cuda being None directly identify a build without NVIDIA CUDA support, explaining why PyTorch cannot use CUDA.

hypotheses.name: NVIDIA driver or GPU visibility may also need checking
hypotheses.rationale: The CPU-only build explains the PyTorch symptom, but the NVIDIA driver and GPU have not yet been checked independently.

missing_information: How PyTorch was installed and whether the environment is virtualized, containerized, or remote
Whether nvidia-smi recognizes the GTX 1080 and the installed driver version

candidate_next_tests.instructions: In the same affected environment, run `python --version` and `python -m pip show torch`. Report the output and whether this is a virtual environment, container, or remote environment.
candidate_next_tests.name: Identify Python version and installation environment
candidate_next_tests.purpose: Identify compatibility and installation details needed to select an appropriate CUDA-enabled PyTorch package.

candidate_next_tests.instructions: Run `nvidia-smi` in a terminal on the same Windows machine and share its output or exact error.
candidate_next_tests.name: Check NVIDIA driver visibility
candidate_next_tests.purpose: Determine whether the NVIDIA driver recognizes the GTX 1080 independently of PyTorch.

diagnosis.summary: The affected environment has a CPU-only PyTorch installation, so this PyTorch build cannot use the GTX 1080 through CUDA.
basis: The installed version is reported as torch 2.14.0+cpu.
torch.version.cuda is None, indicating that this installation has no CUDA build.
The same diagnostic reports CUDA unavailable and zero CUDA devices.

remediation.summary: Use a CUDA-enabled PyTorch build compatible with the Python version and Windows environment, after confirming driver and GPU visibility.
requirements: Determine the Python version and environment type.
Check whether nvidia-smi recognizes the GTX 1080 and identify the installed driver version.
Confirm the appropriate PyTorch build and supported driver requirements for the identified versions before installation.

research_request.reason: Collect the Python version and NVIDIA driver details first; exact version information is needed for focused compatibility research.
